title: Jurisdictional Access Proof Collector and Retention Orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a platform component (Proof Collector) to assemble, sign, and retain jurisdictionally scoped access evidence bundles for audit and periodic review. The collector will ingest RBAC snapshots, SCIM delta exports, SSO assertion traces, session events, and periodic access review outcomes; apply retention policies per-tenant/region; cryptographically sign bundles; and expose automated evidence upload endpoints for compliance teams and auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Collector produces a per-tenant bundle that contains: RBAC role mappings, last 90-day SCIM change log, SSO assertion hashes for exported timeframe, and reviewer decisions for periodic reviews
Bundles are stamped with zone-of-residency metadata and cryptographic signature (KMS/HSM integration)
Retention policy configuration allows per-tenant overrides and enforces automatic deletion/archival after TTL
Compliance dashboard shows bundle generation status, size, residency tag, and last-signed timestamp
Evidence export API returns pre-signed download URLs with audit trail and enforces tenant-scoped IAM
End-to-end test demonstrates a simulated auditor pulling a signed bundle and verifying signature using public key
tasks: Design proof bundle schema (flat files + manifest) and residency metadata model
Prototype SCIM delta replay consumer that can reconstruct user-to-role timelines
Instrument SSO assertion trace exporter to include assertion hash and timestamp
Implement retention policy evaluator with per-tenant overrides and grace window
Integrate with KMS to sign bundle manifests and store signature reference
Expose evidence export API with RBAC checks and usage quotas
Build minimal compliance dashboard card and alerting for failed bundle runs
Add regression tests and a local end-to-end demo harness
notes: Trade-offs: including full assertion payloads increases bundle size and PII surface; we will prefer assertion hashes + pointer to archived raw assertions (if tenant opts in).
Decisions: use existing SCIM reconcile stream (ENG-70555) as source-of-truth for delta snapshots; avoid large DB migrations by streaming to S3 archive for bundle assembly.
Open question: retention legal minima vary by jurisdiction; product must expose configurable retention presets and labels for legal/compliance to select per-tenant.
Operational concern: signing throughput under peak (daily per-tenant bundles) could stress KMS quotas; plan to batch signing requests and rotate ephemeral keys where possible.
Privacy note: redact PII fields by default in exported bundles unless tenant has explicit opt-in and TOS acknowledged.
changelog: 2025-01-07: Initial design doc and schema draft completed. Aisha created Confluence spec.
2025-01-15: Spike for SCIM delta consumer succeeded; mock bundles assembled locally (Morgan).
2025-01-22: Security asked to review signing approach; scheduled KMS integration review on 2025-02-03.
2025-02-03: KMS review notes - prefer envelope encryption and signing via HSM-backed keys; updated design.
2025-02-10: First end-to-end prototype runs nightly for 3 tenants; retention evaluator flags one tenant with expired evidence and queued archival job.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: schema + SCIM/SSO instrumentation + KMS signing spike (2 sprints). Phase 2: retention evaluator, export API, dashboard card (2 sprints). Phase 3: hardening, multi-region residency tagging, and legal presets (1 sprint). Rollout to pilot tenants behind feature flag with audit logging enabled.
risk_mitigation: Limit initial pilot to 3 tenants and run signed bundles to a secure archive in a single region. Monitor KMS usage and implement exponential backoff on signing. Keep original raw events for 30 days before deletion to support forensic reassembly.
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema validation and redaction rules. Integration tests for SCIM delta replay and SSO trace ingestion. End-to-end smoke that creates bundle, signs it, verifies signature, and simulates auditor download. Add chaos test for KMS outage to verify graceful fallback (retry and alert).
